mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה requires הדר for an אתרוג, the לולב of an אשרה, and a לולב with a cut or split top
overview: This עמוד opens with the end of רבי יהודה's proof that dry species are כשר, and the חכמים answer that what people do under pressure (שעת הדחק) proves nothing. The גמרא then explains why a ברייתא needed to say 'do not add to the four species' and 'do not substitute another fruit for a missing אתרוג.' Next it brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה allows an old אתרוג, which refutes רבא's claim that רבי יהודה requires הדר for an אתרוג. The גמרא defends this conclusion against three sources: a green אתרוג and a very small one are unripe, and a very large one might fall when switching hands. For רבי יהודה, the word הדר in the פסוק means a fruit that stays on its tree from year to year, not a beautiful one. The גמרא then explains why a לולב of an אשרה is פסול even though רבא allows a לולב of עבודה זרה after the fact: this אשרה must be burned, so it counts as already burned and too small. Finally, רב הונא rules that only a לולב whose top is cut off is פסול, not one whose top is split. A challenge to him from a ברייתא begins at the end of the עמוד and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof from city dwellers who passed down old לולבים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view that dry species are kosher. He points to city dwellers who left their לולבים to their grandchildren.
steps.simpleTranslation: [There was a case] with city dwellers, who would pass down their לולבים to their grandchildren!
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the story רבי יהודה tells as proof that a dry לולב is still kosher. People in the cities kept the same לולב for generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לולב passed down to grandchildren must be completely dried out. If people used such לולבים, then dryness does not make a לולב פסול. רבי יהודה treats their practice as evidence for his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: People of the big walled cities, far from where the four species grow
Bequeath, pass down as an inheritance
Their grandchildren
Dry (species)

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד starts in the middle of a sentence. The story began on the previous עמוד with 'אמר רבי יהודה: מעשה' ('רבי יהודה said: there was a case').

phrases.english: involving city dwellers,
phrases.notes: Continuation of רבי יהודה's story from the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: who would bequeath their lulavim
to their grandchildren!
phrases.notes: After so many years, these לולבים were certainly dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּבְנֵי כְרַכִּין, שֶׁהָיוּ מוֹרִישִׁין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's ruling (on the previous עמוד) that dry species are kosher.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that dry species are כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of city dwellers who passed their לולבים down to their grandchildren

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: emergency practice is no proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that what people do in a time of need does not show what the הלכה normally is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? A pressing situation is not a proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's proof. The city people had no fresh לולבים available, so they had no other choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rested on the idea that people used dry לולבים as a normal practice. The חכמים say it was only a fallback, because fresh species were not available. Under normal conditions, a dry לולב would still be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (rhetorical: 'that proves nothing')
A pressing, emergency situation

steps.whyThisMatters: 'אין שעת הדחק ראיה' ('a pressing situation is no proof') is a general principle. A practice adopted only under pressure cannot set the standard for normal times.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there proof from there?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: A time of pressing need is not a proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ (לָהֶם): מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה? אֵין שְׁעַת הַדְּחָק רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The disagreement itself (dry species) stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The practice happened only out of necessity, so it does not show the normal הלכה.

steps.title: Attempt to prove רבי יהודה allows a dry אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to suggest that רבי יהודה allows even a dry אתרוג. That would mean he does not require הדר for the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says even dry ones are kosher. Doesn't that refer to the אתרוג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its larger question: does רבי יהודה require an אתרוג to be beautiful (הדר)? It suggests that his words 'even dry ones are kosher' include the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מיהת' means: set aside the argument about the proof story; look at the ruling itself. A dry אתרוג is not beautiful. If רבי יהודה allows it, he must not require הדר for an אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches (focus on the core ruling)
Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)
Citron, one of the four species
Beauty requirement (from 'פרי עץ הדר')

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף יְבֵשִׁין כְּשֵׁרִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even dry ones are fit.
What, is it not referring to an etrog!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the proof debate and uses רבי יהודה's ruling itself to answer the earlier question about הדר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling 'אף יבשין כשרין' ('even dry ones are kosher'), read as including the אתרוג

steps.title: No: רבי יהודה was speaking about the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יהודה may have allowed only a dry לולב, not a dry אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof by limiting רבי יהודה's ruling to the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof story was about לולבים, so his ruling can easily refer to לולבים alone. Nothing here shows he would allow a dry אתרוג. The question is not settled yet: step 11 brings a clearer source (an old אתרוג) that does settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggestion)
Palm branch

phrases.english: No, it refers to a lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling 'even dry ones' can refer only to the לולב.
steps.whatToRemember: There is no proof that רבי יהודה allows a dry אתרוג. His 'even dry ones are kosher' may refer only to a לולב.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: do not add to the four species
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא: just as you may not take fewer than four species, you may not add more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Just as one may not take fewer of them, so too one may not add to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line from the earlier ברייתא, to examine it. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the מצוה is exactly four species: no fewer and no more. Quoting the line prepares the next step, where the גמרא asks why this needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an earlier source to discuss it)
Diminish, take fewer
Add

phrases.english: The Master said:
Just as one may not diminish from them,
so too one may not add to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, analyzing a line from the earlier ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not add a fifth species to the four species.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to state something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for stating the obvious. The next step will explain why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists four species, so adding a fifth plainly seems wrong. A ברייתא should not waste words, so the גמרא wants to know what this line adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (why say it?)

phrases.english: Is that not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the rule in step 5 needed to be stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'אין מוסיפין עליהן' ('one may not add to them')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so stating it appears unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought an unbound extra species doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires the לולב to be bound together. So we might have thought an extra, unbound species is simply ignored. The ברייתא teaches that it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since רבי יהודה said a לולב needs binding, if one brings another species, this one stands by itself and that one stands by itself. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake the ברייתא prevents. Without this line, we might think adding an unbound species causes no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, binding (אגד) defines the מצוה set. An extra species left outside the bundle might seem irrelevant, as if it stands apart. The ברייתא tells us that bringing it still counts as adding and is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a wrong assumption)
Binding the species together
Stands by itself, separate
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא states the rule without naming anyone. The גמרא explains its need using רבי יהודה's view that a לולב requires binding.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
Since Rabbi Yehuda said
a lulav requires binding,
and if one brings another species,
this one stands by itself
and that one stands by itself,
it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a reasonable wrong assumption that the ברייתא comes to reject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the bundle defines the מצוה, an extra unbound species is irrelevant and allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even an unbound extra species is forbidden as an addition.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Do not add' is needed because, under רבי יהודה's binding requirement, we might have thought an extra species outside the bundle doesn't count.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: no substitute for a missing אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line: if you cannot find an אתרוג, do not bring a pomegranate, quince, or anything else instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If one did not find an אתרוג, he should not bring a pomegranate, a quince, or anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא to examine it. It is setting up the same kind of 'why say it?' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule forbids substitutes: no other fruit may stand in for a missing אתרוג. Quoting it prepares the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Pomegranate
Quince
Anything else

phrases.english: The Master said:
If one did not find an etrog,
he may not bring a pomegranate,
nor a quince, nor anything else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No other fruit may substitute for a missing אתרוג.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again challenges the ברייתא for stating the obvious. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pomegranate is not an אתרוג, so it obviously cannot fulfill the מצוה. Why would the ברייתא need to forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious! (the same challenge formula used in step 6)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the rule in step 8 needed to be stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule forbidding substitutes for an אתרוג
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different fruit obviously does not fulfill the מצוה, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A substitute might make people forget the real אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought a substitute is a good way to keep the מצוה remembered. The ברייתא forbids it, because people could end up using substitutes even when real אתרוגים are available.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let him bring one, so the law of אתרוג won't be forgotten. It teaches us otherwise, because sometimes harm comes from it, since people may come to rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the rule is not about fulfilling the מצוה. It is about whether a substitute could be used as a reminder. The answer is no, because it can lead to harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken thought: a pomegranate would serve as a memorial (זכר) so people don't forget the אתרוג. The ברייתא rejects this, because the reminder itself may become a habit. People could end up taking the substitute even when a real אתרוג is available.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him bring
So that it will not be forgotten
Damage, harm
To be drawn after, become habituated

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody thought a pomegranate fulfills the מצוה. The question was only whether to bring it as a reminder.

phrases.english: Lest you say: Let him bring one,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי שֶׁלֹּא תִּשָּׁכַח תּוֹרַת אֶתְרוֹג,
phrases.english: so that the law of etrog will not be forgotten,
it teaches us otherwise,
because sometimes damage comes from it,
since people may come to be drawn after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לַיְיתֵי, כִּי הֵיכִי שֶׁלֹּא תִּשָּׁכַח תּוֹרַת אֶתְרוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a reasonable wrong assumption (a substitute as a memorial) and rejects it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bring a substitute fruit as a reminder, so the מצוה of אתרוג isn't forgotten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidden, because people may come to use the substitute even when a real אתרוג is available.
steps.whatToRemember: A substitute fruit may not be used even as a reminder, because the reminder could replace the real מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a well-meant 'זכר' (memorial) practice can be forbidden when it risks replacing the real מצוה.

steps.title: An old אתרוג: רבי יהודה allows it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where the חכמים disqualify an old אתרוג but רבי יהודה allows it. This challenges רבא, who said everyone agrees an אתרוג needs הדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An old אתרוג is unfit, and רבי יהודה says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to test what רבא said. It shows רבי יהודה allowing an old, dried-out אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old אתרוג is no longer beautiful. If רבי יהודה allows it, he does not require הדר for an אתרוג. That goes directly against רבא's claim that רבי יהודה agrees an אתרוג must be הדר.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof or a challenge
An old אתרוג, from last year, that has dried out
Rules it fit (kosher for the מצוה)
Unfit, cannot be used for the מצוה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An old etrog is unfit,
phrases.notes: An old אתרוג has dried out and lost its beauty.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבא's earlier claim and tests it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that even רבי יהודה requires an אתרוג to be הדר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An old אתרוג is not beautiful. If רבי יהודה still allows it, he does not require הדר for an אתרוג.

steps.title: רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a conclusive refutation of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבא. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the challenge. רבא's view cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רבא. The conclusion is that רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג. Everything that follows next tests this new conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation: the view is rejected with no answer
The אמורא whose view is being refuted here

steps.whatToRemember: The final view is that רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבא (who is refuted here) with רבה (who is quoted later, in step 18). They are two different אמוראים.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rava,
it is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the challenge from step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's view is rejected. According to רבי יהודה, an אתרוג does not need to be הדר.

steps.title: A green אתרוג: רבי יהודה disqualifies it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new conclusion from a משנה where רבי יהודה disqualifies a leek-green אתרוג. That seems to be because it is not beautiful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really not require הדר? But we learned in a משנה: an אתרוג that is green like a leek, רבי מאיר says it is fit and רבי יהודה says it is unfit. Isn't that because he requires הדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on what it just concluded. It brings a משנה where רבי יהודה is strict about a green אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A green אתרוג does not look like a proper, beautiful אתרוג. If רבי יהודה disqualifies it, it seems he does require הדר after all. That would contradict what was just concluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Beauty: the requirement that the אתרוג be beautiful (from 'פרי עץ הדר')
But didn't we learn in a משנה: introduces a contradicting source
Like leeks: dark green in color
Rules it unfit

phrases.english: And does he not require beauty?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
An etrog that is green like leeks:
Rabbi Meir deems it fit,
and Rabbi Yehuda deems it unfit.
Is it not because he requires beauty?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא בָּעֵי הָדָר? וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה disqualifies a green אתרוג. The obvious reason seems to be that it lacks beauty.

steps.title: Green means unripe, not unbeautiful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a green אתרוג is disqualified because the fruit is not fully ripe, not because it lacks beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because the fruit has not finished ripening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a different reason for רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leek-green אתרוג is not yet a finished fruit. רבי יהודה disqualifies it for being unripe. This has nothing to do with הדר, so the conclusion from step 12 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The fruit has finished growing (is fully ripe)
No: rejects the suggested reason

phrases.english: No, it is because the fruit did not finish ripening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an alternative reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה disqualifies a green אתרוג because it is not הדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He disqualifies it because it is an unripe fruit.

steps.title: A small אתרוג: רבי יהודה requires the size of an egg
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second challenge. רבי יהודה requires a minimum size of an egg, while רבי מאיר requires only a walnut. Is that because of הדר?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: What is the minimum size of a small אתרוג? רבי מאיר says the size of a walnut. רבי יהודה says the size of an egg. Isn't that because he requires הדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source to show that רבי יהודה requires הדר. This time the source is about a very small אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sets a larger minimum size than רבי מאיר. One might think this is because a tiny אתרוג is not beautiful.

keyTerms.meaning: Minimum required size
The size of a walnut
The size of an egg

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The minimum size of a small etrog:
Rabbi Meir says: the size of a walnut;
Rabbi Yehuda says: the size of an egg.
Is it not because he requires beauty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, parallel to step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה does not require הדר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His stricter minimum size seems to be based on beauty.

steps.title: Too small means unripe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: an אתרוג smaller than an egg is not a finished fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because the fruit has not finished ripening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer as before. A tiny אתרוג is not yet a fully grown fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's view, an אתרוג below the size of an egg has not finished growing. The size rule is about ripeness, not beauty.

phrases.english: No, it is because the fruit did not finish ripening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 with the same reasoning as step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an alternative reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The minimum size is because of הדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The minimum size is because a smaller אתרוג is unripe.

steps.title: A large אתרוג: רבי יהודה sets a maximum size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a third challenge. רבי יהודה limits how big an אתרוג may be: one must be able to hold two in one hand. Is that because of הדר?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: For a large אתרוג, the maximum is that one can hold two in one hand. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: even if one can hold only one in both hands. What is the reason? Isn't it because he requires הדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third source. Here רבי יהודה sets an upper limit on size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "too unripe" answer cannot work here, because a big אתרוג is certainly fully grown. So the challenge is stronger: maybe an oversized אתרוג is disqualified because it is not beautiful.

keyTerms.meaning: In a large one: the maximum size limit
A תנא who allows even a very large אתרוג
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And in a large one, the limit is that one can hold
two in his one hand;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Even one in his two hands.
What is the reason?
Is it not because he requires beauty?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וּבְגָדוֹל כְּדֵי שֶׁיֶּאֱחוֹז שְׁנַיִם בְּיָדוֹ אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to the conclusion. This one cannot be answered with the ripeness reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה does not require הדר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A large אתרוג is fully ripe, so the only apparent reason for a maximum size is beauty.

steps.title: A huge אתרוג might fall when switching hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבה's teaching. The לולב goes in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left. If they are handed over reversed, the person will switch them, and a huge אתרוג may fall and become unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Because רבה said: the לולב is held in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left. Sometimes people hand them to him reversed, and he will come to switch them. Then he may come to make it unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical reason for the size limit that has nothing to do with beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When switching the species between hands, a person briefly holds both together. An אתרוג that is too big is hard to grip, so it may drop and become ruined. The maximum size protects the אתרוג; it is not about הדר. So רבי יהודה's view stays consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא quoted here (not רבא)
Right hand / left hand
To switch them around
To come to make it unfit

steps.whatToRemember: All three sources are explained without הדר. A green or tiny אתרוג is unripe, and a huge אתרוג may fall. So רבי יהודה does not require הדר for an אתרוג.
steps.whyThisMatters: This also teaches the practical הלכה of holding the לולב in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left.

phrases.english: No, it is because, as Rabba said:
The lulav is in the right hand and the etrog in the left;
sometimes they hand them to him reversed,
and he will come to switch them,
and he will come to make it unfit.
phrases.notes: A very large etrog may fall while he is switching hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with a new, practical reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an alternative practical reason (preventing damage)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The maximum size is because a huge אתרוג is not הדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The maximum size exists because a huge אתרוג may fall while the person switches hands and become unfit.

steps.title: Doesn't the Torah say the fruit must be beautiful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if an אתרוג does not need to be beautiful, what does he do with the word הדר in the פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהודה, isn't it written 'הדר' (beautiful)?
steps.whatsHappening: Steps 13–18 showed that רבי יהודה's rules come from other reasons and not from beauty. Now the גמרא pushes back: the תורה itself says 'פרי עץ הדר', so how can רבי יהודה ignore beauty?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers explained why רבי יהודה's rules are not about beauty. That leaves a gap: the פסוק clearly uses the word הדר. The גמרא wants to know how רבי יהודה explains that word if not as a beauty requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: But then / however (opens a challenge)
But it is written! (pointing to a פסוק that seems to contradict)
Beautiful (from 'פרי עץ הדר', Vayikra 23:40)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: He holds that an אתרוג does not need to be beautiful (for example, he allows a dried-out one).

phrases.english: isn't it written 'hadar' (beautiful)?
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק 'פרי עץ הדר'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After every one of רבי יהודה's rules was explained without beauty, the גמרא asks how he reads the word הדר in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that an אתרוג does not require beauty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says הדר, which seems to demand beauty. A view that drops beauty seems to go against the plain verse.

steps.title: הדר means a fruit that stays on its tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads הדר as 'dwelling': a fruit that stays on its tree from year to year, which describes the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word means a fruit that 'dwells' (הַדָּר) on its tree from year to year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה reads הדר differently. To him it means 'dwells', not 'beautiful'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הדר can be read as הַדָּר, 'that dwells'. That describes a fruit that stays on the tree across seasons, as the אתרוג does. So for רבי יהודה the פסוק tells us which fruit to take; it does not set a beauty standard.

keyTerms.meaning: Dwells / lives (a play on the word הדר)
Its tree
From year to year

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה ignores the פסוק. He uses it fully, but to identify the fruit (the אתרוג) instead of to require that it look beautiful.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, הדר identifies the fruit: the one that stays on its tree year to year. It is not a beauty requirement. That is why his rules about green, small or very large אתרוגים needed other explanations.

phrases.english: That means: one that dwells on its tree
phrases.notes: Read as הַדָּר, 'dwelling', instead of הָדָר, 'beautiful'.

phrases.english: from year to year.
phrases.notes: The אתרוג can stay on the tree across seasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק by reading the word differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate reading of the verse (re-defining the word הדר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הדר means 'beautiful', so every opinion should require a beautiful אתרוג.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, הדר means 'dwelling on the tree year to year'. It identifies the אתרוג and does not require beauty.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a לולב of an אשרה or of an עיר הנדחת is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The משנה says a לולב) of an אשרה or of an עיר הנדחת (is unfit).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשרה is a tree worshipped as an idol. An עיר הנדחת is a city whose people were led into idol worship; everything in it must be burned. The משנה says a לולב from either one cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped as an idol
A city led astray into idol worship, whose property must be burned

phrases.english: Of an asheira and of a city led astray.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה, which rules that such a לולב is פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אתרוג discussion and turns to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לולב from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is פסול.

steps.title: Is a לולב of an אשרה really unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with רבא's ruling: a לולב of עבודה זרה should not be used at first, but if it was used, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a לולב of an אשרה unfit? But רבא said: a לולב of idol worship should not be taken, but if one took it, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה can call this לולב פסול. רבא said that a לולב of עבודה זרה still works after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this לולב is פסול: it does not work at all. רבא says a לולב of עבודה זרה is only to be avoided at the start (לכתחילה), but it works if used (בדיעבד). These two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
He should not take it (at the start)
If he took it, it is valid (after the fact)
But didn't (so-and-so) say? (opens a contradiction)

phrases.english: And is a lulav of an asheira unfit?
phrases.notes: This question is leading up to a contradiction with another teaching.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: לוּלָב שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — לֹא יִטּוֹל,
phrases.english: a lulav of idol worship: one should not take it,
phrases.notes: This is לכתחילה: from the start, he shouldn't take it.

phrases.english: but if he took it, it is valid.
phrases.notes: This is בדיעבד: once it's already done, it still counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה line just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a לולב of an אשרה is פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא says a לולב of עבודה זרה works after the fact. That contradicts calling it פסול outright.

steps.title: The משנה means an אשרה that must be burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks of the kind of אשרה the תורה commands משה to burn. Since it must be burned, it counts as already burned, so it legally lacks the minimum size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with the אשרה of משה, whose size is considered crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the משנה to a specific type of אשרה: one the תורה says must be burned. רבא was speaking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אשרה of משה' is the type the תורה tells us to burn ('ואשריהם תשרפון באש'). In הלכה, something that must be burned is treated as if it were already burned to ashes (כתותי מכתת שיעוריה). So the לולב legally has no size at all, and a לולב needs a minimum size. רבא's case is an idol that is not headed for burning, so there the לולב keeps its size.

keyTerms.meaning: The kind of אשרה described in the Torah of משה, which must be burned
We are dealing with
Its size is considered crushed: something that must be burned counts as already destroyed
Required minimum size

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that using an idol is disgusting. The problem is size. Because the tree must be burned, the הלכה treats it as ashes already, so the לולב has no valid size.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of עבודה זרה לולב. If it is the kind that must be burned (the אשרה of משה), it is פסול even after the fact, because it counts as already crushed and lacks the minimum size. If not, רבא's rule applies: avoid it at the start, but it works after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule כתותי מכתת שיעוריה (an object that must be burned counts as having no size) shows up across ש״ס wherever a מצוה item needs a minimum size.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with the asheira of Moses,
phrases.notes: The kind the תורה commands to be burned.

phrases.english: whose measure is considered crushed.
phrases.notes: Since it must be burned, it counts as already burned, so it lacks the required size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction by narrowing which case the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה and רבא refer to different types of עבודה זרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's אשרה is the same case as רבא's לולב of עבודה זרה, so the two rulings contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means an אשרה that must be burned. It counts as already crushed and lacks the minimum size, so it is פסול even after the fact. רבא means an idol that is not headed for burning.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording backs up the last answer. The משנה puts the אשרה right next to an עיר הנדחת, so it means an אשרה that must be burned, just like an עיר הנדחת. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording of the משנה is also exact and supports this. It lists the אשרה together with an עיר הנדחת, so the אשרה is like an עיר הנדחת. Learn from this that this is the correct reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the wording of the משנה for the answer in step 23. It then closes that topic with 'learn from this.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא said the משנה means the kind of אשרה that must be burned. Here it points out that the משנה lists the אשרה right next to an עיר הנדחת, and everything in an עיר הנדחת must be burned. Putting the two cases side by side shows that both are things that 'count as already burned.' That is why such a לולב lacks the minimum size and is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording itself supports this point
Since it teaches; introduces the exact wording being pointed to
Similar to; like
A city whose people were led into idol worship; all its property must be burned
Learn from this: a closing formula that accepts the point

steps.whatToRemember: A לולב of an אשרה is פסול because the אשרה must be burned, so it counts as already burned and too small. This is different from רבא's ruling about ordinary עבודה זרה, where a לולב that was used anyway is כשר. The משנה's wording, which puts the אשרה next to an עיר הנדחת, supports this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles how the משנה and רבא's ruling fit together. They are talking about different kinds of עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: It is also precise (in the wording),
phrases.notes: The גמרא is bringing support from the exact wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: since it teaches (the אשרה) similar to a city led into idol worship.
phrases.notes: The two cases are listed side by side in the משנה, so they work the same way

phrases.english: Learn from this.
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the topic

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 23 by pointing to the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה's אשרה is one that must be burned, so it counts as already burned and too small
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists the אשרה next to an עיר הנדחת, whose property must all be burned
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof is accepted. A לולב from an אשרה that must be burned is פסול because it lacks the minimum size.

steps.title: רב הונא: only a fully cut-off top is invalid, a split top is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: a לולב whose top was cut off. רב הונא limits this rule. Only a top that was fully cut off (נקטם) is פסול. If the top only split (נסדק), the לולב is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If its top was cut off' (it is פסול). רב הונא said: They taught this only when it was cut off. But if it was split, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case in the משנה, a לולב whose top was cut off. רב הונא explains how far this rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentions a top that was cut off. רב הונא reads this narrowly: being פסול applies only when part of the top is actually missing. A top that is split is still all there, so רב הונא rules it כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its top was cut off; the tip is missing
They only taught it about; a formula that narrows a rule
Split; cracked open but nothing missing
Valid; may be used for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נקטם and נסדק. נקטם means a piece of the tip is gone. נסדק means the tip is split open but every piece is still there. רב הונא says only נקטם is פסול.

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) Its top was cut off (it is invalid).
Rav Huna said:
They taught (it is invalid) only when it was cut off,
phrases.notes: רב הונא is limiting the משנה's rule to a top that's actually missing.

phrases.english: but if it split, it is valid.
phrases.notes: A split top is still complete

steps.triggerLanguage: נִקְטַם רֹאשׁוֹ. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא נִקְטַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next case in the משנה, after the אשרה discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a לולב whose top is fully cut off is פסול. A לולב whose top is split is כשר.

steps.title: Challenge to רב הונא from a ברייתא about a bent לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a split לולב is really כשר, and starts quoting a ברייתא that begins with a bent לולב. The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a split לולב really כשר? But a ברייתא teaches: A bent לולב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge רב הונא's ruling that a split top is כשר. It starts quoting a ברייתא that will be used against him. This passage ends in the middle of the quote, so the full challenge comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'and is a split one valid?' shows that the גמרא expects a source saying a split לולב is פסול. The ברייתא lists several damaged לולבים, starting with a bent one. The point of the challenge will be clear once the ברייתא reaches the split case.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא; opens a challenge from a ברייתא
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself
Bent; curved over

phrases.english: And is a split (lulav) valid?
phrases.notes: This isn't just a question; the גמרא is challenging what was just said.

phrases.english: But it was taught (in a baraita): A bent lulav,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 25 that a split top is כשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a לולב with a split top is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about damaged לולבים, starting with a bent one, seems to call a split לולב פסול. The full wording comes on the next עמוד.
